title.en: Where Do We Roll Back To?

hints.tr: `current = history[-1][0]`; sonra `for version, status in reversed(history[:-1]):`.
hints.en: `current = history[-1][0]`; then `for version, status in reversed(history[:-1]):`.

hints.tr: Döngüde `status == "ok" and version != current` ise o sürümü döndür; döngü biterse `None`.
hints.en: In the loop, if `status == "ok" and version != current`, return that version; if the loop ends, `None`.

hints.tr:
Çözümün tamamı:

```python
def rollback_target(history):
    current = history[-1][0]
    for version, status in reversed(history[:-1]):
        if status == "ok" and version != current:
            return version
    return None


history = [
    ["1.0.0", "ok"],
    ["1.1.0", "ok"],
    ["1.2.0", "failed"],
    ["1.2.1", "ok"],
    ["1.3.0", "failed"],
]
print(rollback_target(history))
print(rollback_target([["2.0.0", "ok"], ["2.0.0", "ok"]]))
print(rollback_target([["0.1.0", "failed"], ["0.2.0", "failed"]]))
print(rollback_target([["1.0.0", "ok"], ["1.1.0", "failed"], ["1.1.0", "failed"]]))
```
hints.en:
The full solution:

```python
def rollback_target(history):
    current = history[-1][0]
    for version, status in reversed(history[:-1]):
        if status == "ok" and version != current:
            return version
    return None


history = [
    ["1.0.0", "ok"],
    ["1.1.0", "ok"],
    ["1.2.0", "failed"],
    ["1.2.1", "ok"],
    ["1.3.0", "failed"],
]
print(rollback_target(history))
print(rollback_target([["2.0.0", "ok"], ["2.0.0", "ok"]]))
print(rollback_target([["0.1.0", "failed"], ["0.2.0", "failed"]]))
print(rollback_target([["1.0.0", "ok"], ["1.1.0", "failed"], ["1.1.0", "failed"]]))
```
